messages:
ashwin: Pager fired for control-plane rolling maintenance — multiple serving nodes returned 502s across eu-west1 for ~3m. I kicked off the maintenance but alerts spiked earlier than expected. Can folks ack and help triage? @oncall-bot @incident-bot

oncall-bot: [pager] ashwin acknowledged. Incident channel created. Priority: P2. Pager ID: PGR-2026-317111. Escalation: recollect on-call infra. Please paste short impact summary.

ashwin: Impact summary: client requests to hosted API intermittently 502/504, affects short-lived requests and streaming sessions. Estimated affected customer set: <5% of production traffic in eu-west1; most traffic hitting fallback region. No data loss. Rolling maintenance window started as scheduled at 10:00 UTC but a node drain completed earlier than expected and triggered a flurry of reconnects.

maria: Ack. I'm on it — checking router drain logs and kube node termination events. If we can confirm it's a noisy drain we should throttle the drain rate or pause remaining drains until we have graceful reconnects.

joel: Do we need to page SRE infra overlap or open a bridge? I can join bridge if needed. Also, should we post a statuspage update now or wait to confirm scope?

ashwin: Bridge would be useful. Paging infra-sre to join bridge and asking ops to temporarily pause remaining drains. We should post intermediate Status: "Partial Degradation — investigating" so that customers see we're aware. If it stabilizes in 10m we'll update.

incident-bot: Incident created: PGR-2026-317111. Bridge: https://calls.redwood.example/bridge/317111. Paging: infra-sre, netops. Statuspage draft state set to: investigating.

liz: Drafting statuspage and customer-facing note (posting below). Please review edits. We should be conservative on ETA.

liz: ```Statuspage: 10:03 UTC — We're investigating elevated API errors (502/504) impacting a subset of customers in eu-west1 during a scheduled control-plane node drain. We're actively mitigating and have paused remaining drains. Next update in 15 minutes or when we have a rollback/complete plan.```

sam-cs: Thx. For enterprise accounts: please DM me a short paragraph I can paste into our CS tracker. Also, include recommended customer action (retry with exponential backoff; route to fallback region if feasible).

ashwin: Copying short customer DM (for enterprise outreach): ```We're seeing intermittent 502/504 errors that started during a scheduled maintenance in eu-west1. Our engineers have paused the remaining maintenance steps and are mitigating the nodes causing reconnect storms. No data loss is expected. If you rely on managed routing, we recommend retrying requests and routing to another region if you can. We'll keep you updated every 15 minutes until resolved.```

maria: Logs show asymmetric termination sequence for nodes 12-14 — kubelet reported completed but proxy still had active sockets, causing mid-flight requests to fail. I'm escalating to runtime team for quick kernel/proxy checks.

joel: If runtime team confirms a proxy handle leak we should revert this maintenance change and drain with --grace 60s. I can coordinate rollback steps. Who owns the drain script?

ashwin: Drain script is owned by infra-ops (alex). Paging alex now; alex please advise if we can revert to earlier drain behavior or run a targeted rollback.

oncall-bot: alex is out but alex-standby can take. alex-standby acknowledged.

incident-bot: Update: infra-ops engaged. Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) Pause drains for pending nodes, 2) Reconfigure kube-proxy conntrack gc to be more aggressive, 3) Re-run drain with --grace 60s on affected nodes after proxy check. Decision window: 10m.

liz: Updated statuspage draft to include mitigation steps: ```10:12 UTC — Mitigations in progress: paused remaining drains; infra-ops and runtime teams are performing targeted checks and will re-run drains with extended grace once verified.```

sam-cs: Noted. Can we include an estimated next update time in the statuspage post so customers know when to expect the next check-in? 15min is fine.

ashwin: Agreed — next update @ 10:27 UTC. Also adding internal ops template for post-incident follow-up. Liz please add to the incident timeline section.

liz: Internal timeline snippet (paste into the incident doc): ```10:00 UTC — scheduled node drain started; 10:03 UTC — alerts triggered for 502/504; 10:05 UTC — paused remaining drains; 10:07 UTC — infra-ops engaged; 10:12 UTC — mitigation steps initiated; 10:20 UTC — re-run drains on nodes 12-14 with --grace 60s (in progress).```

maria: Kernel/proxy checks complete — we saw stale connections in iptables conntrack table and a backlog in the proxy workers. Re-running drain with --grace 60s now and monitoring.

joel: Re-run complete. Nodes 12-14 drained with the new flags, connection errors have dropped to baseline. Monitoring for 5m.

incident-bot: Metric update: 502 rate returned to baseline for eu-west1 (5m average).

ashwin: Good work everyone. Posting statuspage: transitioning to "Degraded — mitigations successful, monitoring" then we should push a maintenance completion notice when all drains finish gracefully. Liz, pushing the post now.

liz: Statuspage published: ```10:28 UTC — Degraded: Mitigation in place, errors reduced to baseline. We're monitoring and will declare maintenance complete after all remaining nodes drain gracefully.```

sam-cs: Going to reach out to three enterprise customers directly with the DM template and offer a 1:1 update call if they saw issues. Please flag any with higher impact.

ashwin: Action items for handoff and follow-up: - oncall to monitor eu-west1 for 1 hour - infra-ops to run a root-cause follow-up (conntrack/proxy mismatch) - runtime to add a small guard in drain script to verify proxy sockets are drained before node termination - PM to prep comms for affected customers. I'll draft a short RCA skeleton.

liz: I'll post completion notice once we've confirmed last drain. Draft completion notice below for signoff: ```Completion notice: 10:55 UTC — Scheduled maintenance in eu-west1 completed. We experienced a brief elevation in 502/504 errors during node drains due to stale proxy sockets; our teams paused remaining drains, applied mitigations, and re-ran drains with extended grace which resolved the issue. No data loss. Follow-up: a short RCA will be shared in 48 hours with planned fixes to the drain workflow.```

joel: LGTM. Add me as reviewer for the RCA.

maria: Monitoring looks stable. No further spikes in the last 10m. Handing to next oncall: @liz will own monitoring and 1hr watch; @ashwin will own the RCA doc and follow-ups.

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded: liz taking watch until 11:30 UTC.

incident-bot: Incident PGR-2026-317111 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Postmortem task created and assigned to ashwin, runtime, infra-ops.

ashwin: Thanks team. I'll drop the RCA skeleton to #postmortems and ping the PM to schedule a follow-up. Closing thread for live ops; please continue updates in the incident doc if anything changes. :white_check_mark:
